solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Gladly accept healthy, endless orgasm!

indicators.note: Endless means without an end, so the word beside it gives up its final letter before joining in.

blocks.note: healthy is WELL, and an endless WELL has lost its last letter
to come is the crude verb for reaching a climax

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic offer of an unending climax.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops signs almost every puzzle with a word like this one, and the trick is that the crude half sits in the wordplay while the definition stays perfectly polite. The exclamation mark is surface noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome something is to accept it gladly, the verb carrying the pleasure as well as the acceptance.

clue.text: Creepy thing's organ needs an artificial covering

blocks.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a wig is false hair worn over the head

explanation.surface: A creep's organ requiring something false to cover it.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ and covering are both doing suggestive work in the surface, which is the joke; the cryptic reading needs nothing more than an ear and a hairpiece. Earwigs are named for the old belief that they crawl into ears.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig is a small crawling insect, and 'creepy thing' is the nursery way of naming a creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Check cocaine's on the decrease

blocks.note: crack is the smokable form of cocaine
figures on the decrease are down

explanation.surface: Confirming that cocaine use is falling.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack has been the crossword's cocaine since the drug got its street name, and the whole clue reads as a cheerful news bulletin. The answer is the policing that causes the fall, not the fall itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown checks whatever it falls on, taking 'check' in its noun sense of a curb or restraint rather than an inspection.

clue.text: "Load of crooks contributing to Obama fiasco!"

indicators.note: What contributes to something is a part already inside it, so the letters wanted are sitting in the words that follow.

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of ObaMA straight into FIAsco

explanation.surface: A shouted accusation that a gang of criminals helped wreck Obama's record.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks put the words in a mouth, and the mouth is easy enough to guess. A hidden answer thrives on a proper name, because nobody reads a name letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is an organised criminal network, so a load of crooks is a plain if colloquial description of the membership.

clue.text: Lot gets Mike off after e.g. pulling out

indicators.note: Something that has gone off has spoiled and is no longer as it was, letters included.
e.g. is written EG, and pulling those two letters out of the word before leaves the rest behind.

blocks.note: the name as spelt, four of the six letters to be shuffled
GETS with the E and G of e.g. pulled out of it

explanation.surface: Mike being let off the hook once somebody withdraws an example.
explanation.walkthrough: To get someone off is to have them acquitted, and that innocent reading covers an instruction to jumble. The neat touch is that e.g., written out as two letters, is lifted bodily out of GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate, the Turkish word English took whole, and your lot is the same idea: what destiny has dealt you.

clue.text: Elected merely to take on Trump's immigration team? Wrong

blocks.note: a candidate who wins the seat is in
just merely means only
ICE is US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the agency running the deportation drive

explanation.surface: A newly elected member setting out to fight Trump's deportation agency.
explanation.walkthrough: Elected giving IN is worth storing away: a politician who wins a seat is in, and a party out of office is out. The question mark covers the fact that a team here is an agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong, as a noun, is an injustice done to somebody; the words swap in phrases like righting a wrong.

clue.text: Note skimpy attire on male

blocks.note: a mini is a skirt or dress cut very short
M is the standard short form for male, the letter on a form

explanation.surface: Remarking on how little the man beside you is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: A minim is the half-note, worth two crotchets, and one of the few note lengths a setter can actually spell. The surface asks you to picture a man in a very short skirt, which has nothing to do with music.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is one of the written note values of music, so 'note' names the class the answer belongs to.

clue.text: Rather slim hotel boozer in shit, sadly

indicators.note: In names the destination, so the letters just given go inside the ones that follow.
Sadly says the thing is in a sorry state, and letters in a sorry state have fallen out of their proper order.

blocks.note: the four letters of shit in another order, opening up after the first
H is hotel in the radio alphabet
a boozer is a pub, and an inn is the crossword's pub

explanation.surface: The skinny drinker in the hotel bar is sadly in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer in British usage is the pub itself as often as the man propping it up, and the wordplay wants the building. 'In shit' does double duty: the trouble the surface describes and the instruction to go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The -ish ending is exactly the 'rather' of the definition, hedging thin into not-quite-thin.

clue.text: Mean Donald, finally locked up

indicators.note: Finally points at the end of the word beside it, which yields its last letter only.

blocks.note: close means tight-fisted, as in close with money
the last letter of Donald

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted Trump at last put behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Close for mean is the old sense of close-fisted, still heard in 'close with money'. The surface trades on Cyclops's running fantasy of Trump in a cell, while the answer only ever describes a shut door.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed door is shut fast, and anything locked up is closed against entry; the adjective covers both.

clue.text: Dire doctor attending each day – not quite satisfied

indicators.note: Not quite stops just short of the whole word, so its last letter never arrives.

blocks.note: Dr is the everyday abbreviation for doctor
ea is the short form for each, the one used on price labels
d is the standard short form for day
satisfied is FULL, one letter short of it

explanation.surface: A useless doctor calling every day and still leaving the patient unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: Four pieces in eight letters is what makes a charade like this read as a shopping list. EA for each is the piece solvers miss, because it comes off a price label rather than out of Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful and dire are both plain words for very bad indeed, and either will stand in the other's place.

clue.text: Craft that is revealed by addict

blocks.note: a junk is a flat-bottomed Chinese sailing boat
i.e. is Latin's id est, that is

explanation.surface: An addict giving away the trade he is skilled at.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft is one of the crossword's reliable double-edged words, meaning a boat as readily as a skill, and the surface leans on the skill. Junk in its other sense is also slang for heroin, which is where the answer comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Junkie is the slang word for a drug addict, taken from junk as a name for heroin.

clue.text: (&13ac.) What Trump apparently failed to do before bombing Iran, leading to absurd stark messiness

definitions.text: What Trump apparently failed to do before bombing Iran
definitions.note: The definition asks what he failed to do rather than offering a synonym; the thing left undone is the noun phrase itself, which is how a 'what X failed to do' definition works.

indicators.note: What is absurd makes no proper sense, and letters that make no sense are letters out of their right order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

explanation.surface: Trump ordering strikes on Iran without thinking through the chaos that followed.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke needs the news: the strikes were widely reported as ordered in haste, and the answer is the dull paperwork nobody had done. Cyclops takes a phrase from office life and drops it into a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk assessment is the formal weighing-up of what could go wrong before you act, which is precisely what the clue says was skipped.

clue.text: see 12ac.
Coming before one dodgy pseudo religious organisation

indicators.note: Coming before sets the letters it introduces in front of the piece named next.
A dodgy thing is not what it claims to be, and dodgy letters will not stay in the order printed.

blocks.note: the six letters of pseudo in another order
one is the figure 1, written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A shady fake-religious outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Opus Dei is a conservative Catholic prelature, the body The Da Vinci Code turned into a thriller villain, and 'pseudo religious' is Cyclops's dig at it. One for I is a swap worth owning outright.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a personal prelature of the Catholic Church with priestly and lay members, so a religious organisation is what it literally is.

clue.text: "Less than American" journalist could be better employed

blocks.note: under a figure is less than it
US is the standard short form for American
ed is the editor, the crossword's newspaperman

explanation.surface: A reporter dismissed as less than American, when he could be doing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less than American' is the insult, not the instruction, and the quotation marks are there to make it sound like something said out loud about a reporter. ED turns up in these puzzles constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underused is not being employed to anything like its full extent, so it could plainly be better employed.

clue.text: Press turned up – say no more

indicators.note: A thing turned has been swung round to face the other way, so the word beside it is read back to front.

blocks.note: UP taken from its last letter to its first
sh! is the noise that tells someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: Reporters arriving somewhere they shouldn't, with a nudge to drop the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Four letters, two instructions, and the one trap is Press, which looks like newspapers and means shove. SH is spelt the way comics print it rather than the way a dictionary would.
explanation.definitionFit: To push a button and to press one are the same action, and the two verbs swap freely.

clue.text: Adult (not Democrat) rudely interrupts ex-veep – a Trump trait

indicators.note: Not marks the piece to be left out, so the letter it names never reaches the grid.
Someone behaving rudely has no respect for the proper order of things, letters included.
To interrupt is to break in on something already under way, so the letters that interrupt land inside it.

blocks.note: Mike Pence was Trump's vice-president in the first term, and the name splits to let the other letters in
ADULT loses the D of Democrat, and the four letters left come back in another order

explanation.surface: A grown-up breaking rudely into a former vice-president's talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Pence fell out with Trump over the 2020 election result, which is the work 'ex' is doing. The surface promises a grown-up and the definition delivers the opposite of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is childish sulky bad temper, and the clue offers it as one of the traits its target is routinely charged with.

clue.text: Community? Whips not bothered

indicators.note: To be bothered is to be stirred up and unsettled, and unsettled letters do not stay where they were put.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: The party whips shrugging off a question about the community.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip at Westminster is the MP whose job is keeping colleagues voting the right way, so whips not bothered is a picture of discipline going slack. The answer belongs to housing rather than to politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A township is a settlement of people — in South Africa a segregated urban district — and in any of its senses it names a community.

clue.text: Depressed, wife's left – needs an advance

indicators.note: Left here is left as in departed, so the letter it names walks out of the word holding it.

blocks.note: depressed is LOW, and the W that stands for wife has gone
the word itself, taken as two letters

explanation.surface: A man left low by his wife walking out and short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Left is the trap: it reads as what remains and works as what departs. The little word 'an' then sits in the sentence as though it were doing nothing but grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance of money is a loan, the sense used when wages are advanced before payday.

clue.text: Miliband is sentimentally holding views opposed to the official line

definitions.text: views opposed to the official line

indicators.note: What is held is kept inside, so the words beside it have the letters wanted somewhere within them.

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of MilibanD through IS and into SENTimentally

explanation.surface: Miliband getting emotional about views his party would rather he kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led Labour, lost the 2015 election and sits in the cabinet again, so his name brings the party politics the definition wants. Hidden answers hide best across a proper noun, where nobody is reading letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement with the received or official position, whether in a party, a church or a court.

clue.text: Token gains wasted by Labour's leader

indicators.note: Wasted is drunk or wrecked, and what is wrecked keeps neither its shape nor its order.
A leader is the one out in front, so the word beside it hands over its opening letter.

blocks.note: the five letters of gains in another order
the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Labour's leader throwing away the gains the party had made.
explanation.walkthrough: Token gains is a real phrase, which is why the two words look like a unit when they are in fact definition and fodder. The party's leader turns out to be nothing grander than the party's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is an outward sign that something is meant, and a signal is a sign made deliberately to be read.

clue.text: Feature of Balkans aspiring state

indicators.note: A feature of a thing is part of it already, so the letters wanted sit inside the words that follow.

blocks.note: the letters run from the middle of BalKANS into ASpiring

explanation.surface: Something characteristic of the Balkans, where small nations want their own countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a remark about breakaway republics, and nothing in that picture points at America. Hidden words love a long proper noun, and the Balkans supply most of this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is one of the fifty United States, so the definition names the class and the wordplay picks out the member.

clue.text: Political position of the woman revealed in Tonight broadcast

indicators.note: To broadcast is to scatter seed far and wide, and scattered letters come down in no particular order.

blocks.note: what belongs to the woman is hers, and of the woman is her
anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A woman's politics coming out on a television current-affairs show.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonight has been a current-affairs strand on British television for decades, which is what makes broadcast look like part of the programme rather than the instruction. Of the woman for HER is the other quiet swap.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the right is to stand on the conservative wing, a position in politics rather than a place in a room.

clue.text: House Republican's baseball success

blocks.note: a house is a home
R is the letter printed after an American politician's name

explanation.surface: A Republican member of the House of Representatives.
explanation.walkthrough: House Republican is a real Washington job title, printed in every American news report, and the clue simply reads it as two crossword pieces instead of one job.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is baseball's home run, the hit that clears the field and brings every runner home.

clue.text: Initially take exception to embracing politician's allure

indicators.note: Initially asks for initials, the single letter each of the words after it begins with.
To embrace is to get your arms right around something, so what is embraced finishes up inside.

blocks.note: the opening letters of take, exception and to, which then part company to take a passenger
MP is a Member of Parliament, the crossword's default politician

explanation.surface: Someone who objects at first and then warms to a politician's charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Take exception to is a phrase solvers read whole, which is exactly why its three initials are so hard to see separately. The politician then climbs in between two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone and to allure them are the same move: dangling in front of them something they want.

clue.text: A wee disclosure

blocks.note: a wee is British nursery talk for a pee, taken here as a noun
a disclosure is secret information getting out to people who were not meant to have it

explanation.surface: A small piece of news getting out.
explanation.walkthrough: Wee reads as the Scots word for small, and the little joke is that it means the other thing entirely. Two definitions side by side, with no wordplay at all to slow you down.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak is slang for a pee, which is what a wee is, and it is also information escaping to the press, a disclosure.

clue.text: Husband roped into breaks in London feature

indicators.note: Being roped into something is being hauled into the middle of it, so the letter named goes inside.

blocks.note: to break a horse is to tame it, and the word opens after its first letter
H is the standard short form for husband, the letter on a form

explanation.surface: A husband dragged along on short holidays in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaks is the pivot: short holidays in the surface, breaking in a horse in the wordplay. The husband contributes a single letter for all the fuss the sentence makes of him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river London is built on, the feature the city is defined by.

clue.text: Simon had to be sacked, correct?

indicators.note: A sacked man is turned out of his place, and letters turned out of theirs come back in a different arrangement.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Seeking agreement that Simon deserved to lose his job.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark sells correct? as an appeal for agreement when it is doing the definition's work. Sacked for an anagram is the setter's kind of joke: a man turned out of his job, letters out of their order.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish someone is to tell them off for a fault, which is to correct them in the reproving sense of the verb.

clue.text: Lampoon staff residing in Settle

indicators.note: To reside in a place is to live inside it, so the letters named take up residence within the word that follows.

blocks.note: to settle a bill is to pay it, and the word opens after PA
a rod is a staff, the stick carried as a symbol of office

explanation.surface: Employees living in the Yorkshire town of Settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a market town in the Yorkshire Dales, which is why it carries a capital letter, and the wordplay wants the plain verb instead. Staff is the ceremonial stick here rather than the workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody mocks by imitating, and to lampoon somebody is to ridicule them in exactly that way.

clue.text: No faith in diplomat (he is Mandelson)

indicators.note: In says the letters are already sitting inside the words that follow, not to be worked out from them.

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of diplomAT through HE IS and into Mandelson

explanation.surface: Nobody trusting the diplomat, who happens to be Mandelson.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mandelson, Labour's great fixer, served as Britain's ambassador in Washington, which supplies the diplomat of the surface. The bracketed aside looks like a footnote and is where most of the letters are.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is the settled position that there is no God, so having no faith is what the word names.
